'''Richard C. Proto''' (February 9, 1940{{snd}}July 27, 2008)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fold3.com/record/82832156/social-security-death-index-richard-c-proto|title=Richard C Proto|access-date=December 21, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsa.gov/about/cryptologic-heritage/historical-figures-publications/hall-of-honor/Article/1621556/richard-proto/|title=Richard Proto}}</ref> was a noted American [[cryptographer]] and former Director of Research and Advanced Technology at the [[United States National Security Agency]]. He was elected to [[NSA Hall of Honor]] in 2013.

==Early life==

Proto was born and Fair Haven section of [[New Haven, Connecticut]] and graduated from [[Wilbur Cross High School]] in 1958, where he was a member of 1958 team that won the New 
England High School basketball championship in the Boston Garden. Proto then received his bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Fairfield University]] in 1962, and his master's degree in mathematics from [[Boston College]] in 1964.<ref name=GPO>{{cite web|title=155 Cong. Rec. E1269 - Tribute To Richard Proto |publisher=U.S. Government Publishing Office |work=Congressional Record |accessdate=May 7, 2017|url=https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CREC-2009-06-02/html/CREC-2009-06-02-pt1-PgE1269-4.htm}}</ref>

==Cryptography career==

Proto joined the [[United States National Security Agency]] ("NSA") in 1964 as a cryptologic mathematician in the Communications Security Research & Development organization.  He then dedicated the next thirty-five years to the NSA where he served in key roles in the research organization and the operational side of [[information security]], he worked in security component design, security system architectures, vulnerability finding, and risk management.<ref name=NSA>{{cite web|title=NSA Hall of Honor: Richard Proto |publisher=United States National Security Agency |work=nsa.gov |accessdate=May 7, 2017|url=https://www.nsa.gov/about/cryptologic-heritage/historical-figures-publications/hall-of-honor/2013/rproto.shtml}}</ref> Proto eventually served as the NSA Director of Research and Advanced Technology from 1994 to 1999.<ref name=NSA/>

Proto is credited with creating the NSA Applied Mathematics Program to train mathematicians to apply their knowledge to a range of problems beyond the traditional cryptologic mission. He also created the Laboratory for Telecommunications Sciences to focus resources on mastering network technology.<ref name=NSA/> Proto authored 28 technical papers at NSA and was responsible for the invention of several information security devices, two of which were patented in his name.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patents by Inventor Richard C. Proto |publisher=Justia Patents |work=patents.justia.com |accessdate=May 7, 2017|url=http://patents.justia.com/inventor/richard-c-proto}}</ref>

==Awards==

During his career, Proto received the [[Presidential Rank Awards|Presidential Rank Award for Distinguished Service]] and the [[National Intelligence Distinguished Service Medal]]. In 2009, Proto was recognized by the NSA with the naming of the ''Richard C. Proto Symposium Center'' within the NSA compound at [[Fort George G. Meade]] in Maryland. It is only the second time the NSA has formally named one of its facilities.<ref name=GPO/> In 2013, Proto was elected to [[NSA Hall of Honor]] in 2013 for distinguished service to American cryptology.<ref name=NSA/>
